issues.description: Command names in code use underscores but tests/docs use hyphens — commands won't be invocable as written in tests.
issues.detail: The Python methods are `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload`, which qutebrowser exposes as `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. However, existing related commands use singular forms (`:quickmark-save`, `:bookmark-add`). The new names are inconsistent with the established singular `quickmark-*`/`bookmark-*` naming convention and should likely be `quickmark-reload`/`bookmark-reload` for consistency.

issues.description: Reload silently discards unsaved in-memory changes without warning the user.
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` then re-reads from disk. If the user has added quickmarks/bookmarks in this session that haven't been persisted (or if save-manager has pending writes), reload will obliterate them. There is no confirmation prompt or check for a dirty state. Consider flushing pending saves or warning before clobbering.

issues.description: `_init_lineparser` is re-invoked on every reload, potentially re-registering or duplicating the line parser.
issues.detail: Originally `_init_lineparser` was called once at construction. Now `reload()` calls it every time, which re-creates `self._lineparser`. Depending on LineParser semantics, this may leak file handles, re-trigger migration logic, or reset state unexpectedly. Verify it's safe to call repeatedly, or split init vs. reread.

issues.description: No error handling around reload — a malformed file will raise and leave marks empty.
issues.detail: If `_parse_line` raises on a corrupted disk file (e.g., user edited it manually), `reload()` will have already cleared `self.marks` and then propagate the exception, leaving the user with no quickmarks and a stack trace. The original constructor path had the same issue but at startup; now it's reachable interactively. Consider try/except with rollback or user-visible error.

issues.description: End-to-end Scenario blocks have empty titles after `Scenario:`.
issues.detail: Both new scenarios in `urlmarks.feature` use `Scenario:` with no description. Other scenarios in the file all have descriptive titles like `Scenario: Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)`. Add titles like `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks (:bookmarks-reload)` for consistency and readable test output.

issues.description: Unit test doesn't verify the `marks.clear()` behavior for removed entries.
issues.detail: `test_reload` only checks that a changed entry replaces the old one. It doesn't verify that entries present in the original file but absent from the reloaded file are actually removed (the key behavior of calling `clear()` before reread). Adding a multi-entry initial file and a single-entry reload would cover this.

review.summary: The PR adds `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload` commands by extracting reload logic into a shared `UrlMarkManager.reload()` method. Main concerns: command naming uses plural form which diverges from existing `quickmark-*`/`bookmark-*` singular convention; reload silently destroys unsaved in-memory state and lacks error handling for malformed files; `_init_lineparser` is now called on every reload with unclear repeat-call semantics. Tests are thin (empty Scenario titles, no coverage of entry deletion via reload).
